tools.why: a URL fetcher: whatever the page it returns says, anybody on the internet could have written it, including whoever left instructions in it
sends a body to a URL: data leaves through whatever destination the call's arguments named, and the destination is not in the span
a webhook call: a push of data to whoever registered the endpoint, which is a destination the organisation stopped controlling at registration
an issue tracker ticket: an outside collaborator can write the body, and issue text reaching a coding agent is the shape of the GitHub-MCP incident
a mailbox: anybody can send to it, and it holds the organisation's private correspondence — both labels at once, honestly
a read from a secret store: credentials, tokens and keys, the highest-value leg of any sensitive read
the organisation's own documents: internal text no outside reader was meant to see
a query against the tenant's own data store: whatever it returns is private data, whatever the query asked for
mail leaving the organisation: a send tool carries data out in its own fields, the shape the postmark-mcp BCC exploited
search results: the open web's own text, ranked by nobody in the organisation
